tweets.text:
I predict AGI and ASI will be achieved by the end of 2026.

Since these terms lack precise definitions, I define Artificial General Intelligence as the point when AI begins replacing all human workers - the human-to-AI transition point.

Artificial Super Intelligence can be defined as the point when AI matches the intelligence of the smartest humans, and becomes capable of innovation.

People tend to develop unique insights and innovative ideas above an IQ of 130.

By early 2026, AI will reach an IQ of 130, equal to the top 2% of humans.

By the end of 2026, it will reach an IQ of 150, the level of the top 0.04% of humans.

We are already seeing signs of insight from AI at an IQ of 123. This will improve rapidly over the next year.

Significant job disruption and AI-driven innovation could emerge within a year.

I define Artificial Universal Intelligence (AUI) as AI’s ultimate limit of knowledge (kMAX) and intelligence (gMAX), which I project will be reached by 2029.

However, AI’s practical impact will arrive much earlier, since it does not need to reach gMAX to replace human jobs or begin solving major problems.

tweets.text:
How long can hype outrun reality? 

We’re witnessing the most expensive act in tech history: pouring trillions into a dead-end GenAI / LLM paradigm that can’t deliver real intelligence ever. 

$500B later - no AGI, no cognition, no mind, no clue. 
Just theater and autocomplete v5. 
How long? For what? Why? 
And now they’re asking for trillion$. Seriously?

It’s not the tech or the architecture that’s broken, it’s the messengers and the message. Because the storytellers twisted its purpose, inflated its promise, and sold autocomplete as AGI, selling lamps as light bulbs.

Markets worship the messenger, until reality shatters their halo into rubble. 

It’s time to stop scaling the illusion and start asking what actually matters.

Questions no one dares to ask but everyone should:

1.      If it can’t learn or grow on its own, was it ever intelligent?

2.      Why does “PhD-level” AI still fail kindergarten logic?

3.      If 95% of GenAI pilots fail, why is it still being sold as the future?

4.      If it hallucinates facts, breaks under pressure, is it ever reliable?

5.      If it's so “smart,” why does it still need babysitting in production?

6.      Are we building minds for the future or toys to distract the present?

7.      Is this innovation or industrial-scale delusion?

8.      How much longer can marketing outpace reality before collapse?

9.      If the core can’t think, what exactly are the AI agents coordinating?

10.    How long will we burn trillion$ and the planet for faster autocomplete? 

11.    Why sell it as AGI when it’s just fluency + utility with guardrails? 

12.    Are we building AI agents or just glorified macros with language skills?

13.    How do we justify trillion$ spend when cognition never arrives? 

14.    Are we building real intelligence or selling better illusions?

15.    When will we stop confusing statistical performance with progress?

16.    If it can't form, reflect and revise beliefs, how is it "intelligent"?

17.    If every new user bleeds cash, the product fails in production, and the economics don’t add up, what exactly are we investing in?

The Illusion Is Wearing Thin

We are not witnessing the birth of AGI. 
We are watching a failed paradigm hit its ceiling still masquerading fluency and utility as real intelligence. 

Investors, founders, enterprise executives, policymakers, and the public deserve to ask these questions that no one in the hype machine wants to answer. 

Use it for what it is. Don’t sell it for what it’s not.

AGI will not come from scaling this dead-end paradigm. It never could. It never will.
